title: Mini observability onboarding kit for new engs
content:
Purpose:
A compact onboarding kit for new engineers joining anything that touches the inference path: serving-runtime, routing, kv-cache, and Console dashboards. The goal is: first 90 minutes = be able to locate the right dashboard, run one synthetic probe, and open an actionable investigation ticket. First day = add or tweak a low-risk metric and get it showing up on a dev dashboard.

Audience:
- New hires on eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-sre, and solutions engineering.

Scope / assumptions:
- This is a pragmatic minimal set, not an exhaustive instrumentation standard.
- Focused on token-serving flows (text generation/chat/embedding paths).
- Assumes access to internal dashboards, tracing UI, and telemetry repo.

Quick start (first 90 minutes):
1) Sign into Console -> Observability -> Dashboards -> "Dev: Inference Health (Compact)" (alias link provided in Confluence).
2) Run the synthetic probe: /ops/probes/run?probe=inference-echo-dev. Expect success within 2s; if not, capture trace id.
3) Find a recent failed request: filter failures by "fallback_rate > 0" and grab trace anchor.
4) Create an investigation ticket (ENG-XXXXX), paste the trace link + 3 screenshots: global latency histogram, per-stage timing waterfall, and model execution histogram.

Priority metric skeleton (minimal required for first-week ownership):
- request_count: per-route, per-tenant, 1m/5m rolls (tagged: route, tenant, deployment).
- request_errors_total: include 4xx/5xx split and identify fallback_count.
- p50/p95/p99_latency_ms: broken into stages (ingress, routing, execute_start->execute_end, token_emit).
- token_emit_rate: tokens/sec per model_variant.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: prefix cache hit / lookup_count (tenant-scoped).
- batch_size_p50/p95: batching behavior; important for cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- cold_start_rate: percentage of requests that had cold KV cache (proxy for warmup).
- fallback_rate_per_1k: fallbacks to smaller model or CPU path per 1000 requests.

Metric naming & tags guidance (short rules):
- Metric names are snake_case, nouns (no verbs), and end with _total/_count/_ratio/_ms/_rate where applicable.
- Tags: route, tenant_id (hashed), model_variant, region, kernel (e.g., cuBLAS, custom-op), batch_policy.
- Keep cardinality low: prefer coarse model_variant tags (e.g., gpt-7b.q8) rather than full commit hashes.

Tracing anchor points (minimum spans to add or verify):
- span.ingress.receive (includes request.headers, route)
- span.routing.policy_decision (policy, chosen_model_variant)
- span.kv_cache.lookup (hit|miss boolean, prefix_key_hash)
- span.dispatch.to_gpu (queue_time_ms)
- span.model.exec (kernel, seq_len, batch_size)
- span.token.emit (first_token_ms, last_token_ms)
- span.fallback.trigger (fallback_to, reason)

Trace tag schema (recommended):
- trace_id, span_id, parent_id (auto)
- tenant_id: hashed (sha256:8)
- route: string (e.g., /v1/generate)
- model_variant: short string
- kernel: short string
- batch_id: short id

Sampling policy (starter proposal):
- Default: probabilistic 0.5% for successful low-latency requests.
- Conditional capture: full traces (100%) when failures or fallback flags are set.
- Dynamic amplification: if p95 latency for a route rises above threshold -> escalate sampling to 10% for 30 minutes for that route.
- Retention tiers: short traces (7d) for full-sample; long-tail anomalies placed in 30d TTL.

Dashboard wireframes (dev-focused):
1) Dev: Inference Health (Compact)
   - Top row: global request_rate, error_rate, p95_latency (single numeric + trend)
   - Mid: per-route small-multiples of p95 and kv_cache_hit_ratio
   - Bottom: a lightweight waterfall panel: last 10 slow traces (click-through to trace UI)
2) Model Execution Portrait (Dev)
   - Histogram: model.exec duration by model_variant
   - Scatter: batch_size vs latency (each point clickable)
   - Kernel selector: filter by kernel and region

Oncall runbook snippets (for new engs):
- If global p95 spikes > 2x baseline: check router policy changes (recent rollouts), then check capacity (GPU pool saturation), then kv_cache heatmap.
- If fallback_rate rises: look for model variant rollout commit, check disk IO (if KV on-disk) and kernel failure counts.

Typical small changes new engs can do safely:
- Add a derived metric: batch_size_p95 via existing histogram (no code deploy if we can fold server-side metric).
- Lower cardinality of a tag by mapping user_subroute -> route (in router layer) and re-instrument with the mapped tag.
- Tweak sampling rate for a noisy dev route in the sampling config repo (telemetry/sampling-config).

Checklist: first week tasks
- [ ] Verify Dev: Inference Health (Compact) dashboard is visible and can be queried.
- [ ] Run synthetic probe and record baseline metrics.
- [ ] Create or own one SLI: (eg. kv_cache_hit_ratio for /v1/embed).
- [ ] Implement one small metric or tag cleanup and send PR to telemetry repo.
- [ ] Pair with an oncall rotation to observe real incidents.

Open questions / decisions to raise:
- Target sampling amplification thresholds: should escalation be trigger on absolute latency (ms) or on relative delta to 7d baseline? (pros/cons in notes).
- Should model_variant tag include quantization profile? (adds cardinality)
- TTL policy for traces from enterprise tenants (regulatory requirements may differ).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add example queries for common investigation recipes (SQL snippets).
- Draft a small PR template: telemetry change must include expected cardinality delta and heat impact.
- Coordinate with product-hosted-api for standardized route naming.

References and quick links:
- Confluence onboarding page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/obs-infra-onboarding
- Sampling config repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/sampling
- Slack channel: #obs-ops (use thread tag "onboard-<your-name>")

Final note (why this is different):
This document is deliberately small and prescriptive for ramping new engineers quickly. It avoids full metric taxonomies and instead focuses on the minimal, high-leverage signals and first-actions that lead to an investigation. Keep feedback coming — will expand into a fullized playbook once we validate the first-week checklist in three onboard cycles.

Authors: Priya Narang (owner), Ethan Cole, Marta Rivera, Liam O'Connor
